live-20260908-health.title: Lending account check
live-20260908-health.brief:
This comparison uses a saved data snapshot, not current trading instructions. Use a normal calculator or spreadsheet, without AI or a marketplace agent. Show calculations, conclusions and limitations. Do not transfer funds.

Using the public lending account below, determine whether its health factor crosses the 1.25 alert threshold and calculate the USD repayment needed to reach a target of 1.5.
Health factor = collateral USD value × weighted liquidation threshold ÷ debt USD value.
Allowed debt at target = collateral USD value × weighted liquidation threshold ÷ 1.5. Repayment = debt − allowed debt; use zero if negative.
Alert if the health factor is below 1.25; otherwise continue monitoring. Explain why this does not guarantee against future liquidation. This account is not your wallet.

live-20260908-grid.title: Grid price plan
live-20260908-grid.brief:
This comparison uses a saved data snapshot, not current trading instructions. Use a normal calculator or spreadsheet, without AI or a marketplace agent. Show calculations, conclusions and limitations. Do not transfer funds.

Using the observed pool price, calculate nine geometrically spaced price levels between the supplied bounds and the USD allocation per level.
Price at level i = lower bound × (upper bound ÷ lower bound)^(i ÷ 8), for i from 0 to 8. Budget per level = total budget ÷ 9.
List all nine prices, rounded to two decimals. Explain whether the configured maximum drawdown has been automatically enforced and what is still required before placing real orders.
The USD 1,000 budget, ±5% bounds and nine levels are task assumptions. USDT is assumed to equal USD 1. Fees, slippage and gas are unknown; do not calculate net profit.

live-20260908-yield.title: Compare two deposit yields
live-20260908-yield.brief:
This comparison uses a saved data snapshot, not current trading instructions. Use a normal calculator or spreadsheet, without AI or a marketplace agent. Show calculations, conclusions and limitations. Do not transfer funds.

Using the two observed Venus rates, compare expected net income on USD 10,000 over 30 days, then rank the risk-adjusted results. APY is an annualized rate in percent based on current rates, not a guaranteed return.
Net income = 10000 × [(1 + APY ÷ 100)^(30 ÷ 365) − 1] − 0.09.
Adjusted income = net income − |net income| × risk score ÷ 125. Calculate both venues and rank from highest adjusted income to lowest.
Risk scores 22 / 18, USD 0.09 cost, budget and duration are task assumptions. Total value locked was not read; the zero in the input means unknown, not an actual zero deposit base. Explain why this estimate alone does not justify depositing or guarantee profit.
